solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bearing skyward aboard a mostly modern European rocket

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so one piece is carried inside the other
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: modern means new

indicators.note: in a down clue, going skyward means reading upwards, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a person's bearing is their air or manner

explanation.surface: A navigator's heading points up into the sky from aboard a European space launcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' means manner here, not a compass direction; 'skyward' turns it to RIA, which goes 'aboard' the A and the trimmed word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariane is the name of the European Space Agency's family of launch vehicles.

clue.text: Mountaineer's final farewells, leaving European range

indicators.note: final points to the closing letter of the word before it
leaving means one piece departs from the other, so its letter is taken out

parts.note: farewells are goodbyes, French adieus

explanation.surface: A climber's last goodbyes as they leave a mountain range in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A radius is the distance something reaches, its range or scope, as in a delivery radius.

clue.text: Edge unbristles tip of beard imperfectly, leaving this?

definitions.text: Edge unbristles tip of beard imperfectly, leaving this?

indicators.note: imperfectly suggests the letters are not set out properly, so they are rearranged
the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A razor edge shaves a beard badly and leaves a fashionable rough growth behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange EDGE, UNBRISTLES and B (the tip of 'beard'); the whole clue also describes the result of a careless shave.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately cultivated short facial growth results when shaving leaves bristles only partly removed.

clue.text: Good person representing Spock and women's rearing state

indicators.note: in a down clue rearing means rising up, so the whole string is read from the bottom

parts.note: Leonard Nimoy played Mr Spock in Star Trek
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A nice actor who played Spock and some women raise a rumpus about a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearing' reverses G + NIMOY + W as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyoming is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Mountain West.

clue.text: Walking into motor oil company, runs into reduced cost of fossil fuel

parts.note: a motor is a car

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: BP is the British oil company
walking means going on foot
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the word into taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Someone walks into a motor oil firm and complains about the falling price of fossil fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walking' goes 'into' the car and oil firm, between the B and P; 'reduced' cuts the second 'into' to INT.
explanation.definitionFit: The total greenhouse emissions from burning coal, oil and gas is the environmental price of using them.

clue.text: Ace regiment's up in school, working to a higher degree

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a school of whales is also called a pod

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
RGT is the abbreviation for regiment, with the possessive S kept

explanation.surface: A crack regiment rises in a school, its members studying for advanced qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses A + RGT + S to STGRA, which goes into POD; school here is a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: A postgraduate student, shortened form, is studying for a master's or doctorate after a first degree.

clue.text: Having lost one's shirt? Otherwise one hopes for worthwhile payback

parts.note: with the shirt gone, a person is left in a vest
otherwise means or, an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone who has lost their shirt, a gambler ruined, contrasts with one expecting a good return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost one's shirt' is the idiom for losing all one's money, but here it is literal: in a vest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts money into a venture does so expecting a profitable return on it.

clue.text: Ignoring repeats, Barney Rubble changed in suave manner

indicators.note: changed signals the remaining letters are rearranged
ignoring repeats means every letter that has already appeared is skipped, keeping one of each

explanation.surface: A cartoon caveman, Barney Rubble, transformed into someone polished and smooth.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNEY RUBBLE minus its second R, B, B and final E leaves BARNEYUL, which 'changed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbane means smooth and courteous, so the adverb describes acting with suave polish.

clue.text: Steed added to Emma's ultimate value

indicators.note: added to places this piece after the previous one
ultimate means the last letter of the word

parts.note: a steed is a horse, a mount

explanation.surface: John Steed of The Avengers is linked to Emma Peel's ultimate worth.
explanation.walkthrough: Steed and Emma Peel were partners in the British TV series The Avengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A quantity or sum, as in the amount owed, is a value.

clue.text: Pharaoh partly got over stroke

indicators.note: got over suggests turning over, so the letters read backwards
partly means only part of the word is used

explanation.surface: An Egyptian ruler partially recovered from a stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' takes RAO from inside Pharaoh and 'got over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In rowing, the stroke is the crew member setting the pace, and any rower can be called by the name of the blade they pull.

clue.text: Writing a condition, I limit turning to non-violence

indicators.note: turning means the whole sequence is read backwards

parts.note: MS, manuscript, is a piece of writing
if introduces a condition
a cap is a limit, as in a spending cap

explanation.surface: Someone writes a stipulation, capping their own urge to turn to violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses MS + IF + I + CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacifism is the belief that war and violence are never justified, a principled rejection of force.

clue.text: Reinforce part of name Philip shares with his mother

definitions.meaning: to strengthen with strips of wood, as in fixing hatches down

definitions.text: part of name Philip shares with his mother
definitions.meaning: Prince Philip took the surname Mountbatten; his mother was Princess Alice of Battenberg, and the two names share a middle portion

explanation.surface: A clue about strengthening part of a royal family name shared by mother and son.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Philip, husband of Elizabeth II, anglicised his mother's family name Battenberg to Mountbatten.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten or strengthen with wooden strips, as in securing a hatch, is a verb meaning reinforce.

clue.text: Pariah soon interrupts ditty beset by piano mistakes

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the inner piece sits within the outer

parts.note: errata are mistakes, especially in printing

indicators.note: interrupts means breaks into, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a ditty is a simple song
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: An outcast soon cuts short a little tune that is spoiled by wrong notes on the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupts' and 'beset by' nest one piece inside another twice; 'piano' is the musical marking for soft, giving one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally an unwelcome person, the Latin phrase describes someone shunned or excluded, an outcast.

clue.text: Whisky and bitter by mouth

indicators.note: by mouth means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: wry means bitterly ironic or sardonic

explanation.surface: A whisky with a bitter taste on the tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of whiskey distilled mainly from that grain, popular in North America.

clue.text: Composer of some art?

indicators.note: a composer arranges things, so the following words are put together in new order

explanation.surface: A question asking who creates a bit of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer of' signals rearranging SOME ART; the whole clue also defines a great musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguished conductor or musician who creates musical works is honoured with this title.

clue.text: Maybe porter holds a barrow, allowing freedom of choice

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
a barrow is a small cart

explanation.surface: A railway porter grasps a barrow, free to choose where to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' flags porter as an example of ale, not the luggage carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering from the menu item by item, rather than set courses, lets diners pick freely.

clue.text: Very well-upholstered article goes in time of revolution

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: goes in signals that the article is placed inside the other word

parts.note: jokingly, well-upholstered means plump, lardy
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A very plush armchair article enters during a time of political upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests uprising but means the Earth's rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: The time taken for the Earth to rotate once relative to the sun, a full spin on its axis.

clue.text: Report of collision energy in parched ground?

parts.note: pow is the sound of an impact

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: parched means dry
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: The bang of a crash and energy released over dry, cracked earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun (earth) but is the past participle of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something milled or crushed finely becomes like dust or fine particles, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Stage regular parts for Meg Ryan

indicators.note: regular parts means every other letter is taken from the words

explanation.surface: A theatre director offers stage roles regularly to the actress Meg Ryan.
explanation.definitionFit: A period or phase of history or development, such as the Victorian period, is a stage.

clue.text: A couturier initially involved in composed lines

definitions.text: A couturier initially involved in composed lines

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so these letters go into the other word

parts.note: lines composed as poetry are verse

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter

explanation.surface: A fashion designer is first mentioned in a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: A and C go inside VERSE between S and E; the whole clue describes Gianni Versace.
explanation.definitionFit: Gianni Versace was a famous Italian fashion designer who founded the luxury house bearing his name.

clue.text: Money-holder, keeping rest, wasted rand among money for financial disaster

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside

parts.note: a wallet holds money

indicators.note: wasted means wrecked, so the letters are rearranged
among places one letter inside the other word

parts.note: cash is money
R is the abbreviation for the rand, South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: A wallet with some money left, and South African currency squandered amid cash: a money disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' gives STRE, which 'keeping' places inside the money-holder; 'among' puts the rand's letter in the money. The rand is South Africa's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1929 stock market collapse in New York triggered the Great Depression, a classic financial catastrophe.

clue.text: Man races to stop rare, exotic hunting dog

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so this piece goes inside
exotic means strange, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle races

explanation.surface: A man races to stop a rare and exotic hunting dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' gives RAER and 'to stop' plugs the races into it; 'Man' is the Isle of Man, home of the TT motorcycle races.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier or other dog bred and used for catching rodents, killing rats.

clue.text: Bloodhound picked up end of trail in hot third day

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means lifted, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, on taps

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the other piece

parts.note: Tuesday is the third day of the week counting from Sunday, short form Tues

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter

explanation.surface: A tracking dog finds the end of a scent trail on a hot Tuesday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' sounds like a homophone signal but is a reversal: L goes into H TUES, and the lot is turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a detective is called a bloodhound, someone who tracks down culprits doggedly.

clue.text: Sharp movement relating to billion in capital

parts.note: a zag is a sharp change of direction, as in zigzag
re means about or relating to

explanation.surface: A sudden market lurch involving a billion dollars in capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks financial but means a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital city of Croatia.

clue.text: Pom queen swallowing last of Queenslander's fizzy drink

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a Pom, Pomeranian, is a spitz-type dog

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the word

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a queen

explanation.surface: An English migrant, a Pom, and a queen swallow an Aussie's fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Pom is Australian slang for an English person, but here it is the Pomeranian dog breed; 'swallowing' takes in the last letter of Queenslander.
explanation.definitionFit: A long drink of white wine mixed with soda water, sparkling and refreshing.

clue.text: In recession, any other business targets are constricted by me

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: AOB is the standard meeting-agenda abbreviation for any other business

explanation.surface: In an economic downturn, the last agenda item is that business targets get squeezed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' and 'targets' suggest economics; the definition speaks as the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A large snake kills prey by coiling round and squeezing it, so its victims are constricted by it.

clue.text: Christian missionary left America retaining suitable backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the whole string is reversed
retaining means holding inside

parts.note: US is America
apt means suitable

explanation.surface: A missionary leaves America, keeping the right kind of support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but signals the whole wordplay read backwards, with 'retaining' holding suitable inside America.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle to the Gentiles travelled widely spreading the early Christian faith.

clue.text: What may litter church steps etc if not tidied up

indicators.note: if not tidied up, the letters are reorganised into a new order

explanation.surface: Mess on church steps after a wedding, if nobody sweeps it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steps etc' reads naturally, but ETC begins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Small paper pieces thrown over a newly married couple are often left strewn outside the church.
